newsitem.title: UK: British Gas silent on contract renegotiation level.
newsitem.headline: British Gas silent on contract renegotiation level.

text.p: British Gas declined to comment on Thursday on the price at which it had agreed to renegotiate its take-or-pay long term gas contracts with both British Petroleum Co Plc and with British Gas Exploration and Production.

Roy Gardner, chief executive designate of Centrica Plc, which will unite British Gas Trading, British Gas Services, British Gas Energy Centres and trading company Accord Energy, said only that the contracts had been renegotiated at "a market level."
But he added at a press conference that "the market level is not the spot price."
Another senior British Gas excecutive said the market level reflected both the production cost of gas from the North Sea and the price in continental Europe, which itself is related to the oil price.
Gardner denied that the timing of the current announcement had any connection with the fact that spot prices have recovered in the second half of this year.
"You can't read too much into current spot prices as the market's too shallow, but it's a good thing that they've come up," he told Reuters.
Gardner denied a suggestion that Accord Energy had been partly responsible for the rise in spot gas prices since the beginning of this year.

Under the new organisation of Centrica, the same holding company will own both Accord and the Morecambe fields, but Gardner denied that Accord had deliberately moved the market in the knowledge that it would take on Morecambe gas, or that the long shutdown of Morecambe over this summer was a deliberate attempt to move prices.
"Accord has had no responsibility for influencing spot prices," he said.
David Varney, chief executive designate of BG Plc, declined to comment on speculation that the average price paid by British Gas under its long-term contracts was 16 pence a therm.

Chairman Richard Giordano said the current renegotiation agreements, covering 2.8 billion therms over five years at a cost of 293 million stg, represented around 10 percent of the problem "we want to attack."
But he added that this was not the same as 10 percent of all long-term contracts, as British Gas was happy with the prices of some of them and had no wish to renegotiate them.
